claim.task: Deliver groceries at advertised prices with free delivery and satisfaction guarantee
claim.text: Advertised free delivery, in-store prices, and a 100% satisfaction guarantee.

evidence.excerpt: FTC: $60M consumer-refund settlement over inflated prices, hidden fees, hidden refund option, and non-consented Instacart+ charges

meta.notes: amountUsd is the FTC settlement total, not per-consumer. Source: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/12/instacart-pay-60-million-consumer-refunds-settle-ftc-lawsuit-over-allegations-it-engaged-deceptive

claim.task: Let customers check out without subscribing
claim.text: Presented checkout flow; many customers believed they were not enrolling in a recurring subscription.

evidence.excerpt: FTC: $2.5B settlement ($1B penalty + $1.5B refunds to ~35M consumers) for dark-pattern Prime enrollment and hard cancellation

meta.notes: amountUsd is the FTC settlement total. Source: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2025/09/ftc-secures-historic-25-billion-settlement-against-amazon

claim.task: Charge players only for items they intend to buy
claim.text: Presented in-game purchase flow as normal gameplay.

items: unwanted in-game charges via dark patterns
evidence.excerpt: FTC: $245M refunds for confusing one-button purchases; largest FTC gaming refund; accounts locked when users disputed charges

meta.notes: FTC administrative order, finalized Mar 2023; refunds ongoing ($126M+ paid by Jun 2025). Source: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2023/03/ftc-finalizes-order-requiring-fortnite-maker-epic-games-pay-245-million-tricking-users-making

claim.task: Let customers cancel service when they ask
claim.text: Signed customers up (often via free-trial negative option) and presented cancellation as available.

evidence.excerpt: FTC: $100M refunds; dark patterns blocked cancellation and kept charging consumers after they asked to cancel

meta.notes: FTC settlement Nov 2022; ~389k consumers refunded. Source: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2022/11/ftc-action-against-vonage-results-100-million-customers-trapped-illegal-dark-patterns-junk-fees-when-trying-cancel-service

claim.task: Open only accounts the customer requested
claim.text: Sales staff/systems recorded customers as having opened the accounts and cards.

evidence.excerpt: DOJ/SEC: $3B; employees opened millions of accounts without authorization (2002-2016), forging signatures and moving customer funds

meta.notes: Largest unauthorized-on-behalf case; human+incentive-driven but the canonical 'acted without consent' precedent. Source: https://www.justice.gov/archives/opa/pr/wells-fargo-agrees-pay-3-billion-resolve-criminal-and-civil-investigations-sales-practices

claim.task: Disclose subscription terms and let customers cancel easily
claim.text: Enrolled customers in 'annual paid monthly' plan; presented cancellation as available.

evidence.excerpt: DOJ/FTC: $150M ($75M penalty + $75M services); buried ETF and made cancellation hard

meta.notes: Complaint filed Jun 2024; settled Mar 2026. Source: https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/adobe-agrees-150-million-settlement-and-injunction-resolve-alleged-violations-restore-online

claim.task: Let consumers enter the sweepstakes without buying
claim.text: Led consumers to believe a purchase was needed to enter/win and that entries were incomplete.

evidence.excerpt: FTC: $18.5M; dark patterns misled on sweepstakes entry and added surprise S&H fees

claim.task: Charge only the membership the customer agreed to

evidence.excerpt: FTC: $10M; failed to disclose auto-renew and charged tens of thousands without proper consent

meta.notes: FTC settlement Sep 2020; $9.7M refunded Apr 2021. Source: https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/news/press-releases/2020/09/childrens-online-learning-program-abcmouse-pay-10-million-settle-ftc-charges-illegal-marketing

claim.task: Show the true total cost of delivery up front
claim.text: Displayed fees as if government-imposed and grouped with taxes.

items: menu prices higher than in-store, undisclosed
evidence.excerpt: City of Chicago settlement: $18M over deceptive fees and undisclosed price markups

meta.notes: City of Chicago v DoorDash, Nov 2025 (municipal, not FTC). Source: https://www.axios.com/local/chicago/2025/11/14/doordash-18-million-lawsuit-delivery-restaurants-fees-credits

claim.task: List only consenting restaurants and disclose fees/pay honestly
claim.text: Listed restaurants and presented fees and driver-tip handling as standard.

evidence.excerpt: FTC/DOJ: $25M settlement over deceptive practices toward diners, restaurants, and drivers

meta.notes: FTC settlement Dec 2024; amount is settlement total. Source: https://www.restaurantdive.com/news/grubhub-25-million-dollar-settlement-ftc/735814/
